cias, in conferendo concursu Deum sequi

bere, qualem illae exigunt, nihil est. Hinc
enim non sequitur, concursum Dei a causis
secundis determinari, sed hoc tantum se-
quitur, naturam & modum operandi in
causis secundis esse rationem objectivam,
quae talem concursum requirat, qualem
Deus tribuit, sed pro arbitratu suo, sive quia
ita decrevit. Nam quemadmodum Deus
ab aeterno certas res decrevit, certo tempo-

agendi potestate praeditas; ita quoque de-
crevit ab aeterno cum iisdem rebus ad ope-
randum sic concurrere, ut natura singula-
rum postulat.

page.notes: Dark smudge at the top right corner and a short dash at the bottom centre are marks on the scan, not print, so they are left out. The ornamental rule above the chapter heading is a printer's rule and is not transcribed as text. "THESIS I." is set in spaced capitals; I followed the rule for numbered theses and wrote it as a paragraph, not a heading. The initial "A" is a woodcut letter joined to "ctum" as "Actum". The catchword "accidentia" is set at the right with a stroke before it.
